meta_title: Databricks and Snowflake SQL Client for Mac | jplus2
meta_description: Run SQL on Databricks (Azure, AWS, GCP) and Snowflake from a native Mac code editor, next to your code, with no client tool to install.
h1: A Databricks and Snowflake SQL client for Mac, inside your code editor
lead: The full version of jplus2 connects to Databricks and Snowflake through their own SQL APIs. You write the query next to your code, press a shortcut, and read the results in a grid.
card_title: Databricks and Snowflake SQL on a Mac
card_text: Connect to Databricks on Azure, AWS or GCP and to Snowflake from a native Mac editor, and export the results as CSV.

sections.html:
• Databricks on Azure, AWS and GCP.
  • Snowflake.

Both use their own SQL APIs, so there is no command line client to install first. The same SQL tab also works with Azure SQL, SQL Server and Synapse, PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, SQLite files, and Excel and CSV files. The Mac App Store version does not offer the Azure SQL, SQL Server, Synapse, PostgreSQL, MySQL or MariaDB connections.

1. Choose Database ▸ Manage Connections… (⇧⌘D) and add a Databricks or Snowflake connection.
  2. Open a SQL tab and write your query.
  3. Press ⌘↩ to run the selection, or the statement at the caret.
  4. The results appear in a grid under your code. Copy them, or export them as CSV. From version 1.0.1, Export… also saves an Excel workbook (.xlsx) or JSON.

Passwords, tokens and API keys are kept in the macOS Keychain.

sections.h2: Why use an editor for this
sections.html: Notebooks and web consoles keep the query away from the script that uses it. In jplus2 the SQL, the Python or shell code around it, GitHub and the AI assistant are in one window, so you can query a warehouse, adjust a script and commit the change without switching apps.
These connections are part of the full version of jplus2, on the Mac App Store. jplus2 Lite, the free download, does not include SQL.

faq.q: Do I need to install a client tool for Databricks or Snowflake?
faq.a: No. jplus2 connects through their own SQL APIs.
Databricks on Azure, AWS and GCP.
Yes. Copy the grid, or export it as CSV. From version 1.0.1 you can also export an Excel workbook or JSON.

faq.q: Is it in the free Lite version?
faq.a: No. SQL is part of the full version of jplus2.
